# Use Grok to Explain a Confusing News Article in Plain English

> **In short:** Paste a confusing news article into Grok with a short, specific request, and it returns a plain-English summary of who is involved, what happened, and why it matters. Paywalled articles usually have to be copied and pasted manually, since Grok often can't read them from a URL alone.

We've all clicked a headline that sounded important, then bounced off after two paragraphs of jargon. This guide walks you through turning one of those articles into something you can actually understand — using Grok, the AI assistant from xAI. By the end, you'll have a five-minute routine you can repeat whenever a story makes your eyes glaze over.

## Before you start
- **An X account** (the same one you'd use to post on X / Twitter). It's free to create one if you don't have it.
- **A web browser** or the **X app** on your phone — Grok lives inside both.
- **One news article** you want explained. Have it open in another tab or app before you begin.
- **About 5 minutes.** That's the whole routine.
- A free X account works for basic chats. Heavier or longer use may need a paid plan; check Grok's official page for the latest details.

## Step 1 — Open Grok and start a fresh chat
Open a browser and go to **grok.com**, or open the X app and find the **Grok** option. If you're not signed in, Grok will ask for your X account. Once inside, look for a text box near the bottom of the screen, usually labeled something like "Ask Grok" or "Message Grok." Tap inside it to start a new conversation. If older chats are showing, look for a **pencil icon** or a **+ button** to begin fresh; this keeps your new article separate from earlier context. If you're on the X mobile app, the Grok icon usually sits in the middle of the bottom navigation bar — tap it and the chat window slides up.
💬 Example: type a quick "hi" first, just to confirm everything is working, before pasting anything.
You'll know it worked when you see an empty chat box with a blinking cursor, ready for your question.

## Step 2 — Copy the article text
On the page with the article you want explained, select the text. On a computer, click at the start and drag your mouse to the end; on a phone, long-press the first word and drag the highlight bar to the last word. Then choose **"Copy"** — usually from a right-click menu on desktop, or a small pop-up menu on mobile. The words now live on your device's clipboard, ready to paste anywhere. If copying doesn't work on some sites, try your browser's **Reader Mode** or print the page to a PDF, then copy from there. If the article is paywalled, you can usually only copy the visible preview — but that's still better than pasting only the link, because Grok often can't read paywalled pages from a URL alone.
💬 Example: copy the headline, byline, and the first three to five paragraphs — usually enough for a clear summary.
You'll know it worked when you paste the text into any other app (like Notes) and the article words appear there.

## Step 3 — Paste the article and ask for a plain-English summary
Click into Grok's text box and paste your copied text — **Ctrl+V** or **Cmd+V** on a computer, **long-press then "Paste"** on a phone. Right below the pasted text, add a clear instruction asking for a plain-English explanation. Hit **Enter** or tap the **send arrow** (usually a small upward icon next to the box). Grok starts typing a reply within a few seconds — you'll see words appear one by one or in chunks, finishing with a complete summary. If the reply is too short or misses the point, send a follow-up message in the same chat with a more specific prompt. The interface varies slightly between web and mobile, but the basic paste-and-send flow is the same everywhere.
💬 Example: paste the article, then on a new line type: *"Explain this like I'm smart but not an expert. Who is involved, what actually happened, and why does it matter?"*
You'll know it worked when Grok replies with a short, organized summary written in everyday words.

## Step 4 — Ask follow-up questions about the parts you still don't understand
Read Grok's reply. If anything is still fuzzy — a person you don't recognize, a phrase you don't know, or a number that doesn't quite make sense — just type another question in the same chat. Grok remembers the conversation, so you don't need to paste the article again. Watch for the new reply appearing just below your question, usually within seconds. If Grok doesn't have enough information to answer, it will usually say so honestly or ask you to clarify. If the chat window looks frozen, scroll down — sometimes the reply sits below where you're looking. This is where the conversation really starts to feel useful.
💬 Example: *"Who is [Name] you mentioned? Why are they important in this story?"*
You'll know it worked when Grok answers your specific question in plain English, building on the earlier summary.

## Step 5 — Ask for the "why does this matter" angle
This is the step most people skip — and it's the most useful. Ask Grok to connect the dots to your everyday life: why should a regular person care, what might happen next, or what to watch for. Type a short request and send it. Grok will reply with a brief take. Treat it as a starting point, not the final word — news is complex, and Grok's reading is just one view among many. If you want a different angle, simply ask — for example, how a small business owner might read the same story, or how it could affect renters in a city. The free plan covers basic chats; very long sessions may eventually hit a limit, and exact limits change, so check Grok's official page for current details.
💬 Example: *"In two or three sentences, why should an ordinary person care about this story, and what's the most likely next development?"*
You'll know it worked when you can explain the article to a friend in your own words — that's the real test.

## Common mistakes
- **Pasting only a paywalled URL.** Grok can sometimes read public web pages from a link, but paywalled articles often block that — only a short preview loads, or nothing does. The fix: copy the visible text and paste it directly into the chat, even if it is only the first few paragraphs.
- **Asking "explain this" with no context.** A bare "what does this mean?" usually gets a vague reply. The fix: tell Grok who you are and what you want — for example, *"I'm a regular reader, not an expert — please give me the short version and the context."*
- **Trusting the summary without checking key facts.** Grok can sometimes mix up details (this is called a **hallucination** — when an AI confidently states something that isn't actually true). The fix: for anything that affects a real decision, double-check the names, numbers, and dates against the original article or another reliable source.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** the next time a confusing headline crosses your feed — about a new law, a court ruling, a market shift — you have a five-minute routine to actually understand it instead of scrolling past.
- **For your work:** when a colleague shares a dense industry article or a long report, you can pull out the key points quickly and decide whether the full read is worth your time.
- **If you're just getting started:** try this once with one short article before you need it. Build the habit on something low-stakes, so the routine feels natural the next time something genuinely confusing shows up.

## Try it now
Pick one headline from today's news that made you feel a little lost. Copy the first three to five paragraphs, paste them into Grok, and type: *"Explain this like I'm smart but not an expert. Who is involved, what actually happened, and why should I care?"* Two minutes, start to finish.
